cycleSpecificCombination.description: A support-first byte-range audit selected only in-footprint CAL products, then a frozen raw r=5 operator was tested at three anchors. Two NRCB1 standards observed months apart were compared by difference-in-differences on their normalized four-position patterns so intrinsic stellar flux cancelled. Python made the pixel measurements and Node independently recomputed every gate.
cycleSpecificCombination.noveltyClaim: No claim is made that aperture photometry, dither differencing, or standard-star calibration is new. The contribution is the explicit control-first adjudication and claim boundary linking an isolated-star operator failure to a prohibition on reopening a crowded-field distance branch.

similarities: The measurement conversion and aperture radius follow the public calibration code rather than inventing a new photometric scale.
The use of different stars and epochs follows the official multi-class, multi-cycle calibration program.
The concern about temporal PSF variation is already documented in JWST crowded-field photometry work.
differences: RC73 deliberately omitted the official STPSF aperture correction to test whether the simpler raw operator could qualify; its failure is therefore a diagnostic branch, not a competing calibration release.
The cross-star comparison used normalized pattern vectors rather than absolute flux or a fitted target-specific offset.
The experiment had an immutable downstream stop: no result could be propagated to the NGC 3447 detector residual, TRGB, distance, or H0.
nextSearchBoundary: Before claiming improvement, search for analyses that cross-validate per-image STPSF or jump-step corrections on standards excluded from calibration-factor fitting, especially Program 7565 hot standards in F090W and F150W.
